readings.title: The Fire at Taberah and the Lust for Meat
readings.subtitle: The Mixed Multitude Complains and Moses Despairs
readings.text: [Numbers 11:1] And it came to be, when the people were as complainers, it was evil in the ears of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard it, and <dn>His</dn> displeasure burned. And the fire of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned among them, and consumed those in the outskirts of the camp. [2] And the people cried out to Mosheh, and Mosheh prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the fire died down. [3] Then he called the name of the place Taḇ‛ěrah, because the fire of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had burned among them. [4] And the mixed multitude who were in their midst lusted greatly, so the children of Yisra’ěl also wept again and said, "Who is giving us meat to eat? [5] "We remember <dn>את</dn> the fish which we ate without cost in Mitsrayim, <dn>את</dn> the cucumbers, and <dn>את</dn> the melons, and <dn>את</dn> the leeks, and <dn>את</dn> the onions, and <dn>את</dn> the garlic, [6] but now our being is dried up. There is naught to look at but this manna!" [7] Now the manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium. [8] The people went about and gathered it, ground it on millstones or beat it in the mortar, and cooked it in a pot, and made cakes of it. And its taste was as the taste of cakes baked with oil. [9] And when the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell on it. [10] And Mosheh heard <dn>את</dn> the people weeping throughout their clans, each man at the door of his tent. And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned exceedingly. And in the eyes of Mosheh it was evil, [11] so Mosheh said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, "Why have You done evil to <dn>Your</dn> servant? And why have I not found favour in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, to put <dn>את</dn> the burden of all these people on me? [12] "Was it I who conceived <dn>את</dn> all these people? Was it I who brought them forth, that You should say to me, 'Carry them in your bosom, as the foster father carries <dn>את</dn> a nursing child,' to the land which You swore to their fathers? [13] "Where am I to get meat to give to all these people? For they weep before me, saying, 'Give us meat to eat.' [14] "I am unable to bear <dn>את</dn> all these people alone, because the burden is too heavy for me. [15] "And if You are doing this to me, kill me – please kill me, if I have found favour in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, and let me not see my evil!"

readings.title: The Seventy Elders
readings.subtitle: The Spirit Rests Upon the Leaders of Israel
readings.text: [Numbers 11:16] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>"Gather to <dn>Me</dn> seventy men of the elders of Yisra’ěl, whom you know to be the elders of the people and officers over them. And bring them to the Tent of Appointment, and let them stand there with you.</dq> [17] <dq>"And <dn>I</dn> shall come down and speak with you there, and shall take of the Spirit that is on you, and put on them. And they shall bear <dn>את</dn> the burden of the people with <dn>את</dn> you, so that you do not bear it yourself alone.</dq> [18] <dq>"And say to the people, 'Set yourselves apart for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat, because you have wept in the hearing of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, "Who is giving us meat to eat? For it was well with us in Mitsrayim." And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall give you meat, and you shall eat.</dq> [19] <dq>You are going to eat, not one day, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days,</dq> [20] <dq>but for a new moon of days, until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes an abomination to you, because you have rejected <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who is among you, and have wept before <dn>Him</dn>, saying, "Why did we come up out of Mitsrayim?" ' "</dq> [21] And Mosheh said, "The people in whose midst I am are six hundred thousand men on foot, and You, You have said, '<dn>I</dn> give them meat to eat for a new moon of days.' [22] "Could flocks and herds be slain for them, to be sufficient for them? Or could all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to be sufficient for them?" [23] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>"Is the arm of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> too short? Now see whether <dn>My</dn> word meets you or not!"</dq> [24] And Mosheh went out and spoke to the people <dn>את</dn> the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people and placed them around the Tent. [25] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the Spirit that was upon him, and placed the same upon the seventy elders. And it came to be, when the Spirit rested upon them, that they prophesied, but did not continue. [26] However, two men had remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldaḏ, and the name of the other Měyḏaḏ. And the Spirit rested upon them. Now they were among those listed, but did not go out to the Tent. And they prophesied in the camp. [27] And a young man ran and informed Mosheh, and said, "Eldaḏ and Měyḏaḏ are prophesying in the camp." [28] And Yehoshua son of Nun, Mosheh’s assistant from his youth, answered and said, "Mosheh my master, forbid them!" [29] Then Mosheh said to him, "Are you jealous for my sake? Oh, that all the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> were prophets, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would put <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> Spirit upon them!" [30] And Mosheh returned to the camp, both he and the elders of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Plague of Quail
readings.subtitle: The Graves of Craving at Kibroth Hatta'awah
readings.text: [Numbers 11:31] And a wind went forth from <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and it brought quail from the sea and let them fall beside the camp, about a day’s journey on this side and about a day’s journey on the other side, all around the camp, and about two cubits above the surface of the ground. [32] And the people were up all that day, and all that night, and all the next day, and gathered <dn>את</dn> the quail. He who had least gathered ten ḥomers. And they spread them out for themselves all around the camp. [33] The meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, and the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against the people, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> struck the people with an exceeding great plague. [34] Then he called <dn>את</dn> the name of that place Qiḇroth Hatta’awah, because there they buried <dn>את</dn> the people who had lusted. [35] From Qiḇroth Hatta’awah the people set out for Ḥatsěroth – and they were at Ḥatsěroth.

readings.title: The Rebellion of Miriam and Aaron
readings.subtitle: The Vindication of the Humble Servant
readings.text: [Numbers 12:1] Now Miryam and Aharon spoke against Mosheh because of the Kushite woman whom he had taken, for he had taken a Kushite woman. [2] And they said, "Has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoken only through Mosheh? Has <dn>He</dn> not also spoken through us?" And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard it. [3] And the man Mosheh was very humble, more than all men who were on the face of the earth. [4] And suddenly <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, and Aharon, and Miryam, <dq>"You three, come out to the Tent of Appointment!"</dq> So the three came out. [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came down in the column of cloud and stood in the door of the Tent, and called Aharon and Miryam. And they both went forward. [6] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>"Hear now <dn>My</dn> words: If your prophet is of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> make <dn>Myself</dn> known to him in a vision, and <dn>I</dn> speak to him in a dream.</dq> [7] <dq>"Not so with <dn>My</dn> servant Mosheh, he is trustworthy in all <dn>My</dn> house.</dq> [8] <dq>"<dn>I</dn> speak with him mouth to mouth, and plainly, and not in riddles. And he sees the form of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. So why were you not afraid to speak against <dn>My</dn> servant Mosheh?"</dq> [9] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against them, and <dn>He</dn> left. [10] And the cloud turned away from above the Tent, and look: Miryam was leprous, as white as snow! And Aharon turned toward Miryam, and look: a leper! [11] And Aharon said to Mosheh, "Oh, my master! Please do not hold against us the sin in which we have done foolishly and in which we have sinned. [12] "Please do not let her be as one dead when coming out of his mother's womb, with his flesh half consumed!" [13] And Mosheh cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, "O <dn>Ěl</dn>, please heal her, please!" [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>"If her father had but spit in her face, would she not be ashamed seven days? Let her be shut out of the camp seven days, and after that let her be readmitted."</dq> [15] And Miryam was shut out of the camp seven days, and the people did not set out until Miryam was readmitted. [16] And afterward the people departed from Ḥatsěroth, and they camped in the Wilderness of Paran.

readings.title: Spying Out the Promised Land
readings.subtitle: The Twelve Leaders Explore Canaan
readings.text: [Numbers 13:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>"Send men to spy out <dn>את</dn> the land of Kena‛an, which <dn>I</dn> am giving to the children of Yisra’ěl. Send one man from each tribe of their fathers, every one a leader among them."</dq> [3] And by the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> Mosheh sent them from the Wilderness of Paran, all of them men who were heads of the children of Yisra’ěl. [4] And these were their names. From the tribe of Re’uḇěn: Shammua, son of Zakkur. [5] From the tribe of Shim‛on: Shaphat, son of Ḥori. [6] From the tribe of Yehuḏah: Kalěḇ, son of Yephunneh. [7] From the tribe of Yissasḵar: Yiḡ’al, son of Yosěph. [8] From the tribe of Ephrayim: Hoshěa, son of Nun. [9] From the tribe of Binyamin: Palti, son of Raphu. [10] From the tribe of Zeḇulun: Gaddi’ěl, son of Soḏi. [11] From the tribe of Yosěph, from the tribe of Menashsheh: Gaddi, son of Susi. [12] From the tribe of Dan: Ammi’ěl, son of Gemalli. [13] From the tribe of Ashěr: Shěthur, son of Miḵa’ěl. [14] From the tribe of Naphtali: Naḥbi, son of Wophsi. [15] From the tribe of Gaḏ: Geu’ěl, son of Maḵi. [16] These are the names of the men whom Mosheh sent to spy out <dn>את</dn> the land. And Mosheh called Hoshěa the son of Nun, Yehoshua. [17] And Mosheh sent them to spy out <dn>את</dn> the land of Kena‛an, and said to them, "Go up here into the South, and go up to the mountains, [18] and see what <dn>את</dn> the land is like, and <dn>את</dn> the people who dwell in it, whether strong or weak, whether few or many, [19] and whether the land they dwell in is good or evil, whether the cities they inhabit are in camps or strongholds, [20] and whether the land is rich or poor, and whether there are forests there or not. And you shall be strong, and bring some of the fruit of the land." Now the time was the season of the first-fruits of grapes. [21] So they went up and spied out <dn>את</dn> the land from the Wilderness of Tsin as far as Reḥoḇ, near the entrance of Ḥamath. [22] And they went up through the South and came to Ḥeḇron. And Aḥiman, Shěshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anaq, were there. Now Ḥeḇron had been built seven years before Tso‛an in Mitsrayim. [23] And they came to the wadi Eshkol, and cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes. And they bore it between two of them on a pole, also of the pomegranates and of the figs. [24] That place was called the wadi Eshkol, because of the cluster which the men of Yisra’ěl cut down from there. [25] And they returned from spying out the land after forty days.

readings.title: The Evil Report
readings.subtitle: The Fear of the Nephilim and the Lack of Trust
readings.text: [Numbers 13:26] And they went and came to Mosheh and Aharon and all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl in the Wilderness of Paran, at Qaḏěsh. And they brought back word to them and to all the congregation, and showed them <dn>את</dn> the fruit of the land. [27] And they reported to him, and said, "We went to the land where you sent us. And truly, it flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit. [28] "But the people who dwell in the land are strong, and the cities are walled, very great. And we saw the descendants of Anaq there too. [29] "The Amalěqites dwell in the land of the South, while the Ḥittites and the Yeḇusites and the Amorites dwell in the mountains. And the Kena‛anites dwell by the sea and along the banks of the Yarděn." [30] And Kalěḇ silenced <dn>את</dn> the people before Mosheh, and said, "Let us go up at once and take possession, for we are certainly able to overcome it." [31] But the men who had gone up with him said, "We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we." [32] And they gave the children of Yisra’ěl an evil report of the land which they had spied out, saying, "The land through which we have gone as spies is a land eating up its inhabitants, and all the people whom we saw in it are men of great size. [33] "And we saw there <dn>את</dn> the Nephilim, sons of Anaq, of the Nephilim. And we were like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and so we were in their eyes."
